claims.statement: released_wasm_gemm_gnaf_global_optimal : GlobalOptimal Release.wasmProfile Release.gemmProblem Release.costObjective Release.artifactBytes

The Atlas seal's universal-cover check is blind to the byte universe: it is determined by the recorded searchPartitions, candidateFacts identities, and partitionCoverRoot alone, so no proposition quantified over ByteArray follows from it.
claims.note: Hardening lemma. Makes machine-checked the fact that Atlas.seal_implies_universal_coverage (SPEC 15) does NOT follow from the seal check, which is why that declaration is absent rather than derived.
claims.axiomNote: Classical.choice is permitted by SPEC 4 as a Lean core logical axiom. SPEC 4's restriction is that Classical.choice SHALL NOT produce executable witnesses; this is a Prop-level congruence theorem, not an executable witness, so the restriction is not triggered.

claims.statement: Atlas.seal_implies_universal_coverage: a sealed state implies universal sublevel coverage over all profile-valid byte modules.
claims.note: ABSENT BY DESIGN. AT-001 proves it does not follow from the seal check. Deriving it from the seal would be unsound.

claims.statement: Charged-operation lower bound for bilinear 3x3 matrix-multiplication schemes: T >= r + 18, uniformly in the multiplication count r, attained exactly by the naive algorithm at r=27, T=45.
claims.scope: BILINEAR SCHEMES ONLY, not all WebAssembly byte modules.
claims.note: Partial progress toward LB-001, NOT its discharge. Establishes that the open interval 19 <= R(<3,3,3>) <= 23 does not gate the release theorem: the bound is uniform in r, so it holds under every resolution of that problem. Because the objective charges multiplications and additions both at weight one, a low-rank scheme pays for every combining addition (Laderman: 23 mults + 98 adds = 121 charged ops vs naive 45).

claims.statement: GlobalOptimal is stated at full strength: its competitor quantifier ranges over all of ByteArray, and it equals GlobalOptimalOver with the maximal scope.
claims.note: Makes SPEC 1's rule -- 'a theorem scoped only to such a subset SHALL have a different name' -- visible in the types. GlobalOptimalOver carries an explicit scope parameter and is provably weaker when the scope shrinks, so a scope-restricted result can never pass as the release theorem.

claims.statement: The competitor universe of GlobalOptimal is inhabited and both universal clauses fire: the released bytes themselves satisfy the competitor premises, so the statement cannot be satisfied vacuously.
claims.note: Anti-vacuity. A GlobalOptimal proof over an empty competitor universe would be worthless; this rules it out.

claims.statement: SPEC 10.3(1): byte strings within a module-size bound are finitely enumerated, and every competitor whose score lies in a sublevel has its bytes in that enumeration.
claims.note: Discharges the finiteness half of SPEC 10.3. Does NOT discharge UV-001: enumerability is not coverage, and the enumeration is physically unrunnable (256^u exceeds the holographic bound at u>51 bytes).

claims.statement: SPEC 10.3: possible_winner_within_sublevel -- an evaluated competitor whose score does not exceed the baseline's lies within the objective's declared resource bound for that sublevel, and its module byte count is within that bound's module-size coordinate.
claims.scopeLimitation: This CONFINES a competitor given an evaluation of it. It does not produce that evaluation (system_evaluation_rel_complete, outstanding), does not claim every competitor has one, and does not claim the sublevel has been searched (universal_sublevel_coverage, outstanding). Only the score hypothesis is used: Universal.withinSublevel_of_score_le proves the same conclusion without SPEC's five other premises, which is stated so that carrying them verbatim cannot be mistaken for needing them. The bound is the objective's OWN boundOfScore field, so nothing here invents a bound; for Cost.canonicalObjective that field is uniformBounds, making the sublevel genuinely finite in every one of the 36 charged coordinates.
claims.note: The first of SPEC 10.3's six numbered obligations, and the only one this repository discharges. It is what makes the search for a winner a search over a bounded carrier rather than over all of ByteArray -- contrapositively, a module outside the sublevel cannot beat the baseline. It is NOT progress on UV-001: bounding the carrier and covering it are different propositions, and the gap between them is the attained universal lower bound of UOR-GNAF 19.3.

claims.statement: SPEC 10.4: partition_cover_complete -- every byte string a root partition cell denotes is resolved by one of the three terminal verdicts (enumerated exactly, refuted as not profile valid, or dominated by a lower bound the incumbent strictly beats), or the strategy is exhibited reporting a coverage gap on a cell that denotes it.
claims.scopeLimitation: Conditional on root.Denotes bytes. A root cell that denotes almost nothing satisfies this theorem while covering almost no competitor, and Universal.coverLeaves_covers_scope proves such roots exist. There is NO hypothesis on the strategy -- a strategy that gives up is caught in the conclusion, not excluded -- but that is a statement about detection, not about coverage. The dominated disjunct's body is the universal lower bound of UOR-GNAF 19.3 verbatim; this repository builds no inhabitant of PartitionResult.dominated for the release scope, and the theorem only transports whatever a strategy supplies.
claims.note: Strictly stronger than the pre-existing coverLeaves_covers, which reached a leaf without saying what happened there. Turning this into UV-001 (universal_sublevel_coverage) needs two further things this repository does not have: a root cell PROVED to denote every profile-valid byte string of the sublevel, and a strategy with no incomplete leaf -- and the only way to seal a cell too large to enumerate is dominated. Both outstanding.

claims.statement: Full-domain aggregation lower bound: if every raw invocation costs at least k on a charged coordinate, the summed coordinate is at least k times the domain size; and any coordinate lower bound transfers to the score.
claims.scope: ALL competitors (not restricted to bilinear schemes).
claims.note: Universal in scope but NOT tight, so it does not discharge LB-001. See LB-004.

claims.statement: The attainment gap: a lower bound L strictly below the released score S does NOT establish minimality; and conversely an attained bound (S = L) does.
claims.note: Isolates the missing piece of GO-001 in Lean. Paired with attained_lower_bound_is_optimal (UOR-GNAF Theorem 11.1 in scalar form), this proves the INFERENCE from an attained bound to optimality is available; what is missing is an attained bound, not the reasoning step. This is why LB-002 and LB-003, though genuinely proved, do not close GO-001.

claims.statement: The GNAF compiler can emit a module implementing the FULL released GEMM problem (all four arithmetic modes of SPEC 8.2).
claims.scopeLimitation: The compiler targets the i32-only executable subset accepted by Wasm/Validate.lean. Of the four required arithmetic modes, only `modular` with a u32 accumulator compiles. `checked`, `strictFloat` and `exactDyadicRoundOnce` all require an accumulator wider than i32 or a checked-overflow test i32 cannot perform, and are compiled to `unreachable` (trap) rather than to code computing something different.
claims.note: Honest by construction -- the artifact traps instead of lying, and Plan.inReleasedSubset is the decidable predicate excluding those nodes. But it means SPEC 13 Phase B ('construct an input-total scalar GNAF GEMM plan') is NOT achievable with the current compiler/target, so no correct release artifact can be emitted. This is a larger gap in O-6 than the module count suggests.

claims.statement: Plan.inReleasedSubset is inhabited by an actual GEMM plan: gemmWitness classifies the raw ABI header, dispatches on layout class, runs the blocked traversal and i/j loop nest, accumulates the k reduction under the modular-u32 contract, STORES the product into the declared C region, sets the status word and publishes C; it type checks, compiles, validates, and its compilation contains no unreachable.
claims.note: DISCHARGED, and now WITNESSED BY A WRITE. gemmWitness is a concrete 1x1x1 modular-u32 GEMM plan: classifies the raw ABI header, dispatches on layout class, runs the blocked traversal and i/j loop nest, accumulates the k reduction, STORES the accumulator into C via Plan.storeReg, sets status success and publishes C. Proved in-subset, typed, compiled, validated, unreachable-free; the accumulator is exactly (A*B) mod 2^32 (gemmWitness_eval_acc); gemmWitness_writes_C reads the C region back little-endian at the stored width and gets alpha*A*B + beta*C mod 2^32 for the alpha and beta this descriptor declares; gemmWitness_eval_mem_outside is the frame; gemmWitness_eval_out publishes the whole four-cell result; gemmWitness_eval_status is status 0 (success).
claims.scopeLimitation: The witness is a 1x1x1 modular-u32 kernel with concrete operands, which is what SPEC 8.3 asks of an anti-vacuity witness. Three limits: (1) gemmWitness_writes_C is the alpha=1, beta=0 instance -- those are the literals the witness header declares (gemmWitnessAlpha_eq, gemmWitnessBeta_eq) and the plan carries no scaling node, so the general alpha/beta form is NOT proved; (2) it is a statement about Plan.eval, not about the emitted Wasm -- that link is compile_refines, omitted under BI-002/O-6; (3) the witness cell image still has overlapping declared regions (A, B, C element lengths of 4 bytes over one-cell elements, and C's four cells run into the declared status-detail record); Machine.classify checks header literals, kind/mode tags and extent only, so no region disjointness is claimed. SPEC 8.3 anti-vacuity witnesses for every scalar-kind x mode x transpose x layout-class combination remain outstanding under BI-002.

claims.statement: GlobalOptimal is ATTAINABLE: if the admissible set is nonempty and the decider answers on admissible bytes, some byte sequence satisfies GlobalOptimal in full -- all three extensional conjuncts, the evaluation existential with Correct and Feasible, the universal lower-bound clause over all of ByteArray, and the canonical tie-break clause.

What remains is an EXHIBITION problem, not a lower-bound problem. Correct and Feasible were NOT assumed: correct_of_admissible and feasible_of_admissible are proved from the three extensional predicates, because every recorded CostedExecutionObservation carries a FiniteExecution proof and both branch costs are pinned to Cost.traceCost by costExact. claims.statement: The concrete release Decider satisfies DeciderAnswersAdmissible: it returns a completed evaluation on every admissible byte sequence that has one. This is SPEC 10.1's system_evaluation_rel_complete.
claims.note: REOPENED after external audit. It was promoted on Release.decider, which is `noncomputable` and built from Release.evaluateClassically: that function ASSUMES Nonempty (SystemEvaluation ...) and then extracts a witness with Classical.choice. It decodes, validates, enumerates and executes nothing. SPEC 19 excludes noncomputable definitions from the product/proof path and SPEC 6.3 requires executable proof-producing functions to be computable, so this is not a conforming discharge. Correspondingly the completeness theorem takes an existing evaluation as an argument rather than proving one exists. `just releasepath` now fails on that shape. RESOLUTION: Release.decider, Release.evaluateClassically, Release.systemEvaluationRel_{sound,functional,complete}, Release.deciderAnswersAdmissible(_rel), Release.exists_globalOptimal_of_{nonempty,admissible_evaluation}, Release.nonemptiness_iff_admissible_evaluation, Release.seam_decider_complete_on_witness, Release.globalOptimal_of_witness_semantics, Artifact.exists_globalOptimal_of_baseline_semantics and the ten Theorems.release_* results indexed by the decider are DELETED, not relabelled and not retained behind a checker. No replacement evaluator over the witness semantics was substituted. Closing UV-003 requires implementing SPEC 10.1's finite decoder, validator, input enumerator and all-branch explorer as a Universal.Decider and proving DeciderAnswersAdmissible of it.

Non-degeneracy proved: seam_costEvent_not_zero (the .branch charge is nonzero and equals dispatchCharge exactly; every event charges >= 1 rule step), seam_validationSteps_pos, and seam_machine_completes at every raw invocation. systemEvaluation_inhabited then gives exists bytes, Nonempty (SystemEvaluation ...), so the nonemptiness antecedent is satisfiable at this seam and the release theorems are no longer implications with an untestable antecedent.

Release.witnessModule is the smallest GNAF.moduleOf output (correct shape, correct ABI, body `i32.const 0`) and is used ONLY to witness that the costed machine completes. Its own doc states it computes no product. UPDATE (BI-006 revisit): the PLAN-level half is now closed -- Plan.loopReg clamps at loopRegMaxTrips and GNAF.gemmKernel_stepBound_le_maxSteps proves the kernel's static Plan.stepBound (792281624699921518248014643209, about 2^99) is inside 2^320, and GNAF.gemmKernel_steps_le_maxSteps bounds every GNAF evaluation. That says NOTHING about Wasm reduction length: compile_resources bounds emitted code SIZE, not execution. Release section 5.13 now carries the real kernel (Release.gemmKernelModule, gemmKernel_profileValid on a closed literal) and proves the entire machine and evaluation chain -- gemmKernel_machine_completes_of, gemmKernelSystemEvaluationOf -- from exactly two named, unproved propositions: Release.GemmKernelReducesBounded (the termination half of the omitted compile_refines) and Release.GemmKernelReachesTerminal (which is Wasm.validation_progress, OUTSTANDING under O-6). BI-006 stays open because those two are Wasm-execution facts and neither is proved.

Two modules exist and neither is both: Release.witnessModule is evaluable but returns `i32.const 0` and computes no product, so SemanticCorrect is FALSE for it -- which means Release.globalOptimal_of_witness_semantics, though correctly stated and honestly annotated ('conjuncts (b) and (c) are the caller's, and this repository supplies neither'), is a conditional whose antecedent is unsatisfiable at witnessBytes. Artifact.baselineBytes is a real GEMM module with baseline_profileValid proved, but is not known to be evaluable (BI-006). Closing GO-006 needs one module with both properties.

claims.statement: The GNAF plan language can express input-dependent computation: reading a descriptor field from memory into a register, and looping a number of times determined by that register.
claims.note: DISCHARGED. Plan.loadReg (memory->register, dual to storeReg, sharing its addressing) and Plan.loopReg (extent read once from a register) threaded through all six GNAF files. loopReg_trips_from_memory proves a loadReg followed by a loopReg runs the body exactly as many times as the MEMORY WORD says -- the statement the fixed-extent fragment cannot make. gemmKernel_writes_C is universally quantified over M N K i j. The same plan is proved correct at three different shapes (1x1x1, 2x2x2, 1x3x2 rectangular with k != n), which is the evidence the fixed-extent limitation is gone. A GNAF IndexMap has plan-constant coefficients, so addresses are computed into a register by scalarOp and read through IndexMap.idB -- address arithmetic is data, exactly as the extents are.
claims.scopeLimitation: Three limits, all stated in the Lean doc comments. (1) THE TRIP COUNT IS CLAMPED. Plan.eval runs a loopReg min(reg extentReg, loopRegMaxTrips) times, with loopRegMaxTrips = 4294967295. A clamp is forced: SPEC 11.2 requires the static bound Plan.steps_le_stepBound, and no fixed natural number bounds an unclamped register-driven loop, so an unclamped constructor would have made that theorem false. The constant is the released i32 ceiling, which is also maxRawExtent, so the clamp is unreachable for any configuration the released ABI can present and for any register value the compiled i32 locals can represent; loopReg_zero, loopReg_succ, loopReg_eq_loopNest and loopReg_trips_from_memory therefore carry the hypothesis n <= loopRegMaxTrips. (2) THE STATIC COST OF A loopReg IS WORST CASE: its charge is the body charge iterated loopRegMaxTrips times, since the plan text no longer knows the trip count. The certified cost of a plan using loopReg is sound but enormous, and no tighter cost claim is made. (3) EXPRESSIVENESS ONLY. This entry closes the language defect; the plan that USES it is BI-008 (GNAF.gemmKernel, an input-dependent GEMM whose i/j/k trip counts are the header's m/n/k, proved correct for arbitrary m,n,k under the bounds stated there, and exhibited on three different shapes). gemmWitness remains the fixed 1x1x1 kernel of BI-003/BI-005 and is unchanged. Everything in both entries is proved of Plan.eval, not of the emitted Wasm (compile_refines remains omitted under BI-002/O-6).

claims.statement: The GNAF plan language expresses an INPUT-DEPENDENT GEMM: one CheckedPlan, GNAF.gemmKernel, loads m, n and k out of the raw ABI header into registers and runs an i/j/k nest whose every trip count is one of those registers, and after evaluation the declared C region holds the modular-u32 product (A*B)[i,j] for arbitrary m, n, k -- not for one shape fixed by the plan text.
claims.note: DISCHARGED. gemmKernel classifies the raw header (classifyRaw), dispatches on the layout class (dispatchLayout), LOADS the SPEC 8.3 extents at cells 16..23, 24..31 and 32..39 into registers 3, 4, 5 with Plan.loadReg (gemmKernel_loads_extents), runs three nested Plan.loopReg loops bounded by exactly those registers (gemmKernelNest_trips: the outer trip count IS the header word), accumulates one multiply-accumulate per k iteration, deposits each result into C with Plan.storeReg as a four-cell little-endian u32, sets the success status (gemmKernel_eval_status) and publishes C (gemmKernel_eval_out). Proved: gemmKernel_inReleasedSubset, gemmKernel_usesVector = false, gemmKernel_typed (CheckedPlan gemmKernelSig gemmKernelOutSig), gemmKernel_compiles (Wasm.validate of the compiled module), gemmKernel_no_unreachable, gemmKernel_loads_extents, gemmKernel_writes_C (the claim), gemmKernelCore_frame (nothing outside C is written), gemmKernel_C_is_contract_fold (what lands in C is exactly the fold of ArithmeticContract.step for the modular-u32 contract gemmKernelContract, so the reduction is performed UNDER THE DECLARED CONTRACT of SPEC 8.2), gemmKernel_eval_conforms. The same CheckedPlan is then proved correct on three different descriptors: gemmKernel_writes_C_1x1x1, gemmKernel_writes_C_2x2x2 (all four entries) and gemmKernel_writes_C_1x3x2 (a rectangular shape with k != n, all three entries). Only the descriptor differs between them, which is the evidence that the fixed-extent limitation of BI-003/BI-005 is gone. Because a GNAF IndexMap has plan-text-constant coefficients, no map can address A[i,t] = 256 + 4*(i*k + t) when k is loaded; the kernel therefore computes every element address into register 0 with Plan.scalarOp and reads it through IndexMap.idB, whose storeAddr is base + reg 0. Address arithmetic is data in this plan, exactly as the extents are.
claims.scopeLimitation: Six limits, all stated in the Lean doc comments. (1) HYPOTHESES, NOT CHECKS. gemmKernel_writes_C is universally quantified over m, n, k and over the entry memory, but assumes: the configuration conforms to gemmKernelSig (14 registers, 1024 memory cells); m.classify = valid and m.layoutClass = rowMajor (the two continuations the kernel body sits in); the header words at 16, 24, 32 are m, n, k; m,n,k <= loopRegMaxTrips (the released i32 ceiling, so this excludes nothing the ABI can present); and m*k <= 64, k*n <= 64, m*n <= 64 so that A, B and C fit their declared 256-cell regions and are therefore disjoint. The plan does not REFUSE a descriptor violating the region bound -- such a descriptor is simply outside the theorem, and Machine.classify does not check it either. (2) alpha AND beta ARE NOT APPLIED: the kernel computes A*B, the alpha=1, beta=0 instance of SPEC 8, exactly as gemmWitness does; it carries no scaling node. (3) THE DECLARED STRIDES ARE NOT CONSULTED: the kernel assumes the packed row-major layout that Machine.layoutClass selects. A descriptor declaring a non-packed row-major view would still enter the kernel and nothing is proved about it. Layout classes other than rowMajor return status unsupported rather than a wrong result. (4) BATCH = 1: the batch axis is not traversed. (5) A CELL IMAGE, NOT THE ABI BYTE IMAGE: as with gemmWitness, the header and element images are the cell-addressed images Machine.byteAt/leWord read; no claim is made that they equal Gemm/ABI.lean's byte image. (6) Plan.eval, NOT WASM: gemmKernel_compiles says the compiled module validates; relating its execution to Plan.eval is compile_refines, still omitted under BI-002/O-6. Also, the static cost of the plan inherits the worst-case loopReg charge recorded under BI-007, so no tight cost claim is made for it.

claims.statement: CI verifies the exact-SHA build: the authority digest step runs from the directory the checksum file names.
claims.note: FIXED after external audit. `sha256sum -c authority/uor-gnaf.sha256` ran from the repo root while the checksum file names UOR-GNAF-v1-draft.2.md WITHOUT a directory prefix, so the step failed and the workflow stopped BEFORE `lake build`. Exact-SHA build and axiom closure had therefore never been established by CI. Now `cd authority && sha256sum -c uor-gnaf.sha256`.

claims.statement: The SPEC 15 inventory is derived from SPEC.md and checked against the compiled environment, not from a hand-maintained status field.
claims.note: ADDED after external audit showed the claims registry materially understated the proof surface: 10 'outstanding' rows against 36 outstanding SPEC 15 declarations. `just required` parses SPEC 15 and queries the compiled environment: 58 required, 22 discharged, 36 outstanding. Gate steps 4, 5, 8 and 9 now test declaration presence instead of reading model/claims.json.

claims.statement: Release.wasmProfile is backed by the completed pinned Core 3.0 semantics rather than the i32 witness profile, and carries SPEC 7.5's Release.wasmCostTableBody.
claims.note: Raised by external audit. `def wasmProfile := Wasm.unitWitnessProfile`, and the cost table is Wasm.canonicalCostTableUnits rather than SPEC 7.5's Release.wasmCostTableBody. The file discloses both, and wasmProfile_body : wasmProfile.body = wasmProfileBody holds by rfl, but the SEMANTICS backing the profile is the i32 subset. So the syntactic 'for all ByteArray' in GlobalOptimal does not yet range over the authority-required Core 3.0 competitor universe. UPDATE (release-path migration tranche): two things changed and neither of them closes this. (1) Release.wasmProfile is no longer SPELLED as somebody else's non-vacuity witness -- it now names its own body, and Release.wasmProfile_eq_unitWitnessProfile states the identity by rfl so the rename is disclosed rather than mistaken for a strengthening. (2) The released profile now has a Core 3.0 module and BYTES to be applied to: WS-005. What is UNCHANGED is the thing this claim is about -- Universal.ProfileValid still decodes with Wasm.Subset.decode, so the competitor universe is still the subset one, and the cost table still has no vendored conformance map behind it. Migrating Universal.ProfileValid onto Wasm.decode is blocked on the Core execution layer: Universal.SystemEvaluation, Universal.StartsCostedInvocation and Universal.Setting.machine all name Wasm.Module, and Wasm/Core/ has no Config, no Store, no successors and no initialGemmInvocationCosted. Moving ProfileValid alone would leave the release conjunction naming two different modules for the same bytes, which is worse than the disclosed gap.

claims.statement: SPEC 15 Wasm.profile_matches_pinned_revision, at the meaning SPEC 7.1 gives the name: the concrete model and conformance map are identity-bound to the VENDORED revision, and every enabled vendored rule has exactly one mapped Lean declaration.
claims.note: Two conjuncts, exactly as SPEC 7.1 defines the name. (1) IDENTITY BINDING TO THE VENDORED REVISION: every lawful Wasm.Profile, core3AdequacyMap and Wasm.core3VendoredTree carry one commit; the map carries the vendored tree record whose manifestSha256 is the SHA-256 of vendor/wasm-spec/SHA256SUMS, itself the list of digests of all forty vendored files; and RevisionBody.identity and VendoredTreeBody.identity are both injective (structural canonical identity from prefix-free encoding -- no collision-resistance assumption anywhere), so a different revision, or a single different vendored byte, gives a different identity. (2) EXACTLY ONE MAPPED DECLARATION PER ENABLED RULE: one fully qualified Lean name, one map row and one vendored anchor per enabled identifier; no declaration shared by two identifiers; nothing at all for a rejected one. Re-indexed as WasmGemmGnaf.Theorems.profile_matches_pinned_revision.
claims.axiomNote: Classical.choice is permitted by SPEC 4 as a Lean core logical axiom; SPEC 4's restriction is that it SHALL NOT produce executable witnesses. It enters through Lean core's String.ofList_toList, used by Wasm.string_append_left_cancel to cancel the `WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.` namespace prefix when qualifying a mapped declaration name. This is a Prop-level theorem, not an executable witness, so the restriction is not triggered.
claims.boundaryNote: Lean does not read vendor/wasm-spec/. The content binding rests on the literals core3VendorManifestSha256, core3VendoredTree.fileCount and core3RevisionCommit; CM-006 is the tooling claim that recomputes them from CONTENT. What is NOT established, and why WS-001/O-6 stay open: the enumeration cites 73 distinct vendored anchors of the 835 rule-shaped labels the vendored tree defines, so PinnedCoreRuleId is a declared SUBSET of the pinned rule set and is not proved to be all of it; and 320 unexpanded SpecTec ${rule: ...} references remain in the vendored sources, whose .watsup bodies are not vendored, so the anchor check tests rule IDENTITY and never rule CONTENT. SPEC 7.1 places the transcription on the authority side of the boundary; this theorem claims nothing on the far side of it.

claims.statement: The Lean literals Wasm.profile_matches_pinned_revision stands on are recomputed from the vendored CONTENT: the digest of vendor/wasm-spec/SHA256SUMS, the per-file digests of all forty vendored files, the file count, the pinned commit, and every vendored rule anchor the conformance map cites.
claims.note: SPEC 5.1 boundary: xtask CHECKS whether the kernel discharged an obligation, it never DECIDES one. Lean cannot read the tree, so a drifted literal would still elaborate; `xtask vendor` (release gate step 1, `just vendor`) is what stops it reaching a green gate. It also checks the gap-3 direction the kernel cannot: every anchor Wasm.PinnedCoreRuleId.vendorAnchor? cites must be a label the vendored .rst sources actually DEFINE, so an invented rule identifier fails the gate. 73 of 73 cited anchors found. Falsifier M13 plants a flipped digest, an appended line and a deleted entry on a COPY of the vendored tree and requires the real checker to reject each, with the unmutated copy as control.

claims.statement: Constructive duplicate-free enumeration of every lawful raw invocation, with a global choice-free Fintype instance, the classifier-driven valid-input enumeration, and an executable input enumerator with completeness.
claims.note: Closes three SPEC 15 declarations: Gemm.raw_input_finite, Gemm.valid_input_finite, Universal.input_enumerator_complete. the SPEC 15 inventory 22 -> 25 of 58, verified independently. raw_input_finite and input_enumerator_complete are CHOICE-FREE ([propext, Quot.sound]); the instance is global with no hypothesis. Achieving that required reproving List.nodup_range, because the toolchain's goes through List.range_eq_range' and depends on Classical.choice. valid_input_finite DOES carry Classical.choice, inherited from Gemm.classify/refValid in committed code (omega discharges Iff/And/Or classically); no enumeration of the VALID carrier can be choice-free while the classifier is not. Recorded rather than glossed.

claims.statement: The released module has PINNED Core 3.0 BYTES: a 53-byte literal that the complete Core 3.0 decoder accepts, returning exactly Wasm.Core.releaseBaselineModule, which is valid under Release.wasmProfile -- well typed in the amended Core 3.0 judgment and admitted by the profile's own feature matrix, limits, closed import policy and exported ABI.
claims.note: The release path is byte indexed and until now nothing on the Core 3.0 side had bytes at all: Wasm/Core/Profile.lean built releaseBaselineModule as abstract syntax and proved it admitted, but no byte string was shown to BE that module under the pinned decoder. Wasm.Core.decode_releaseArtifactBytes is that equation, by kernel computation on a hand-written literal; there is no encoder anywhere in its import graph, and Wasm.Core.releaseArtifactBytes_declarative reaches the pinned grammar Bmodule through Wasm.decode_sound, which xtask independence checks. Anti-vacuity runs in both directions: Wasm.Core.decode_mutatedArtifactBytes shows the decoder still accepts the same literal with the `gemm` export renamed to `gemn`, and Wasm.Core.mutatedArtifactModule_not_admitted shows the released profile then REJECTS it, so admission is doing work rather than passing everything the decoder returns.
claims.scopeLimitation: THREE limits, all stated in the Lean doc comments. (1) These are NOT the bytes the release path selects: Release.artifactBytes does not exist, selection is open (GO-004), and Artifact.baselineBytes is the subset codec's output -- `#eval Wasm.decode Artifact.baselineBytes` reports .error Fault.opcode, recorded as a MEASUREMENT in Artifact/Baseline.lean because the kernel does not reduce Wasm.Subset.encode. (2) Wasm.Core.releaseBaselineModule computes no GEMM: its body is `local.get 0`. It is the released ABI SHAPE. (3) Universal.ProfileValid does NOT range over these bytes; Release.coreArtifact_profileValid_spec_reading states SPEC 10.1's own reading, whose decoder is Wasm.decode, and discharges it on this artifact, and it is explicitly not offered as a discharge of Universal.ProfileValid. WS-003 stays open.

claims.statement: GNAF.compile emits an i32 literal the pinned Core 3.0 syntax cannot hold, so no total map from the release path's instructions to the pinned ones preserves i32 constants: migrating the compiler to Wasm.Core.Module is a change to the COMPILER, not a translation of its output.
claims.note: A negative result, priced so the next migration step does not discover it by finding a proof that stops closing. GNAF.constI n = Wasm.Instr.i32Const (Int.ofNat n) and Wasm.Instr.i32Const : Int -> Instr, so the release path's i32 literal is UNBOUNDED; 2-syntax.values.spectec fixes syntax iN(N) = uN(N), so a Core 3.0 i32 literal is a u32 (GNAF.no_core_i32_lit_two_pow_32). The gap is reachable from the compiler and not merely present in the type: GNAF.bodyCode appends loadAt e.statusAddr to EVERY compiled body (GNAF.compile_body_mem_statusAddr), CompileEnv.pages is clamped to the hard page limit but the ADDRESSES are not, and GNAF.gapChecked -- the plan `nop`, typed by HasType.nop at an interface declaring 2^30 memory cells -- compiles to a body containing i32.const (2^32) (GNAF.compile_gapChecked_emits_two_pow_32). This is the instruction-level counterpart of Wasm/CoreGap.lean's module-level no_typeidx_preserving_map and no_name_preserving_map, stated about the compiler's own output.

claims.statement: GNAF.compile emits Wasm.Core.Module: CompileEnv carries a < 2^32 bound on its layout, envOf establishes it from the plan's interface, and every address lemma and correctness theorem of GNAF/CompileCorrect.lean is re-proved over the pinned Core 3.0 instruction typing.
claims.note: The obligation BI-009 prices. Two halves, and the second is the expensive one. (a) REPRESENTABILITY: Sig.mem, Sig.scratch and Sig.tables are unbounded Nats and CompileEnv.statusAddr scales them, so envOf cannot manufacture the bound -- either CompileEnv gains a proof field and GNAF.compile gains a hypothesis, or the layout is clamped and every address lemma changes. Clamping by wrapping modulo 2^32 is NOT available: a wrapped address can land inside the declared memory and then the access succeeds at the wrong place, which is a semantic change and not a representation change. (b) TYPING: GNAF.compile_validates is proved against Wasm/Validate.lean's checker; the Core counterpart needs Wasm.Core.validate to accept the emitted body, which needs Core instruction-typing lemmas for every emitted combinator (countLoop, dispatchOn, classifyCode, layoutCode, ...). Wasm/CoreArtifact.lean shows the released ABI SHAPE is expressible and admitted, so the obstruction is the compiler's numeric representation and its proof layer, not the target syntax.

refutedFramings.framing: Closure requires the exact tensor rank of <3,3,3> (open, 19<=R<=23).
refutedFramings.reason: Multiplications and additions are both charged at weight one, so rank is not the binding quantity. Laderman's 23-mult 3x3 scheme costs 23+98=121 charged ops vs naive 45. Truth value invariant across [19,23].

refutedFramings.framing: Closure requires exact minimal-program-size lower bounds, an open circuit-complexity problem.
refutedFramings.reason: Weight-one module bytes creates a minimal-total-cost obligation, not a minimal-program-size one; asymptotic circuit lower bounds are the wrong authority.

refutedFramings.framing: SPEC 10.3's 'finite and exactly enumerable' is false at release scale.
refutedFramings.reason: As literally written it is provable with no computation: a subset of a finite type is finite. The magnitudes are irrelevant to a finiteness claim.
